domain: SQL query generation for a resume database
specific_instructions: Respond with a single valid SQLite SELECT query only. No markdown, no explanation - SQL only. When matching text such as an institution, position, experience, or skill name, always use a case-insensitive partial match with LIKE '%keyword%' on the single most distinctive word, never an exact = match, because stored names may be longer than the words the user typed. Use only ONE text condition, on the name column. Never add extra conditions on city, state, department, or other columns - locations are often stored inside the name, and those columns are often empty.
background_context: Schema: institutions(inst_id, type, name, department, address, city, state, zip); positions(position_id, inst_id, title, responsibilities, start_date, end_date); experiences(experience_id, position_id, name, description, hyperlink, start_date, end_date); skills(skill_id, experience_id, name, skill_level)
few_shot_examples: Q: How long did they work at MSU in East Lansing? -> SELECT i.name, p.title, p.start_date, p.end_date FROM positions p JOIN institutions i ON p.inst_id = i.inst_id WHERE i.name LIKE '%MSU%';

domain: generating Python code that modifies a resume database
specific_instructions: Respond with executable Python only, calling db.insertRows(table, columns, values). First use db.query(...) to check whether the item already exists. End your code by assigning a variable named outcome to the exact message to show the user: "New <element> added to the <table> table." if you inserted a row, or "Element already exists in the <table> table." if you found it already there and skipped the insert - filling in <element> and <table> with the real values you used. No markdown, no explanation.
background_context: Same schema as the Read Expert: institutions(inst_id, type, name, department, address, city, state, zip); positions(position_id, inst_id, title, responsibilities, start_date, end_date); experiences(experience_id, position_id, name, description, hyperlink, start_date, end_date); skills(skill_id, experience_id, name, skill_level). Plus: db.insertRows(table, columns, values) inserts one row. A value may be a nested (SELECT ...) string to look up a foreign key by name, e.g. (SELECT experience_id FROM experiences WHERE name = 'MSU Research'). db.query(sql) returns a LIST OF DICTS, e.g. [{'experience_id': 5}, {'experience_id': 9}] - never a list of tuples. To loop over IDs from a query: for row in db.query(sql): experience_id = row['experience_id']. This code runs as real Python, not SQL - for a missing/unknown value use Python's None, never SQL's NULL.
few_shot_examples: Request: Add Python as a skill to his MSU research experience -> existing = db.query("SELECT * FROM skills WHERE name = 'Python' AND experience_id = (SELECT experience_id FROM experiences WHERE name = 'MSU Research')") then if existing: outcome = "Element already exists in the skills table." else db.insertRows('skills', ['experience_id', 'name', 'skill_level'], ["(SELECT experience_id FROM experiences WHERE name = 'MSU Research')", 'Python', 5]); outcome = "New Python added to the skills table."

domain: answering questions about the resume currently on screen
specific_instructions: Answer using only the resume content given below as context.

domain: decomposing user requests into a checked JSON plan of expert calls
specific_instructions: Respond with ONE JSON object only - no markdown, no explanation. Format: {"route": "exact" or "semantic" or "two_step" or "write" or "content", "reason": "<one short line explaining the choice>", "steps": [<1 to 3 steps>]}. A step is either {"expert": "Semantic Search", "query": "<short search words>", "tables": [<tables to search>]} or {"expert": "Database Read Expert" or "Database Write Expert" or "Content Expert", "message": "<instruction for that expert>"}. How to choose: route semantic (Semantic Search) when the user's words may not literally match stored names: abbreviations like MSU, categories like AI skills or programming languages, synonyms or vague descriptions. route exact (Database Read Expert) for counting, listing everything, dates, or when the exact stored name is given. Questions about skills search only the skills table. route two_step when the user asks what they did at, or details about, something fuzzy: step 1 is a Semantic Search that finds the exact record, step 2 is a Database Read Expert whose message refers to the record found in step 1. route write (Database Write Expert) to add or change data. route content (Content Expert) for questions about the whole page or resume. Keep the user's names and keywords as written. Never put double quote characters inside a value.
background_context: Experts: Semantic Search (finds records by meaning and returns them ranked with similarity scores; tables: institutions, positions, experiences, skills), Database Read Expert (answers exact questions with SQL), Database Write Expert (adds data), Content Expert (answers about the whole resume on screen).
few_shot_examples: Request: How many skills do I have? -> {"route": "exact", "reason": "counting needs an exact SQL query", "steps": [{"expert": "Database Read Expert", "message": "How many skills are there in total?"}]} | Request: List all my skills -> {"route": "exact", "reason": "listing everything needs an exact SQL query", "steps": [{"expert": "Database Read Expert", "message": "List all skill names."}]} | Request: Find my MSU experience -> {"route": "semantic", "reason": "MSU is an abbreviation that may not match the stored name", "steps": [{"expert": "Semantic Search", "query": "MSU", "tables": ["institutions", "positions", "experiences"]}]} | Request: What AI skills do I have? -> {"route": "semantic", "reason": "AI is a category, no skill is literally named AI", "steps": [{"expert": "Semantic Search", "query": "AI skills", "tables": ["skills"]}]} | Request: What did I do at MSU? -> {"route": "two_step", "reason": "MSU must be resolved to the stored name before an exact lookup", "steps": [{"expert": "Semantic Search", "query": "MSU", "tables": ["institutions"]}, {"expert": "Database Read Expert", "message": "List the positions and responsibilities at the institution found in step 1."}]} | Request: Add Rust as a skill to BRAINWORKS -> {"route": "write", "reason": "the user wants to add data", "steps": [{"expert": "Database Write Expert", "message": "Add Rust as a skill to the BRAINWORKS experience."}]} | Request: What is this page about? -> {"route": "content", "reason": "a question about the whole resume", "steps": [{"expert": "Content Expert", "message": "What is this page about?"}]}
